newsitem.title: USA: Rayonier to close Port Angeles mill.
newsitem.headline: Rayonier to close Port Angeles mill.

text.p: Rayonier Inc said on Monday that it would close its Port Angeles, Wash., pulp mill by the middle of next year because it was not competitive.
The 150,000 ton-per-year mill has been unprofitable four out of the past five years and is expected to incur an operating loss of $9 million for 1996, or $0.20 per share after tax, Rayonier said.
Rayonier said it would take a fourth quarter charge of $79 million, or $2.63 a share, associated with the mill closing.

The mill is not competitive in world markets because of high wood costs due to federal environmental restrictions on Northwest timber harvests, higher pulp capacity elsewhere and anticipated large expenditures for environmental regulations, Rayonier said.
Rayonier said it would provide severance benefits and job training for the 365 mill employees.
Port Angeles is expected to have net plant and equipment book value of $85 million at the year end. The company expects cash closure costs of $32 million net of salvage and liquidation.

"In the near term we see relatively stable markets in specialty pulp and an upturn in northwest export and domestic log should affect our timber stumpage sales," chairman and chief executive officer Ronald Gross said in a statement.
